name: Promo 1: diorama scenes, 16:9 hero slides, launch film and Blender import proof
description: Second round of Meshwright v1 launch material (docs/15 section 7), after comparing our kit with ccore's card: their lead images show assets working together (a playable game, Godot imports) and one rich asset per 16:9 slide, while ours shows many small props. This PRD builds, from our own generated GLBs only: (1) a scene composer that places many GLBs on one plinth as a diorama, (2) two diorama layouts (village, harbour) rendered as a 16:9 still and an orbit, (3) a plinth option for single hero renders, (4) 16:9 hero slides in a film style, (5) a 25-30 s launch film, (6) a Blender headless import check that proves the GLBs import and renders them in Blender. Every image must stay honest: geometry is never edited, dioramas are captioned 'arranged by hand, every object generated by Meshwright v1'.

userStories.title: Plinth option for single hero renders
userStories.description: As the owner, I want a single asset rendered on a low plinth (like ccore's farmyard slide), so a hero shot reads as a finished diorama piece.
steps: scripts/showcase_render.mjs: add `--plinth none|round|square` (default none, which must keep today's output byte-identical for the same inputs) and `--plinth-color HEX` (default 0x9ccf7a top) with `--plinth-side HEX` (default 0x8a5a3c). The plinth is a bevelled slab (top colour for a thin top layer, side colour below) sized 1.25x the asset's footprint (x/z extent), thickness 6% of that size, its top at y = 0, receiving shadows. Frame the camera on asset plus plinth.
Add `--aspect W:H` (default 1:1) so a hero can be rendered 16:9 at `--size` width; keep the asset centred slightly right of centre only when `--offset-x F` is given (default 0).

Tests (tests/js/showcase_render.test.mjs, Chromium): render a makeGlb two-box asset with --plinth none and assert the PNG is identical to a render from before the change (generate the reference in the same test run by calling the default path twice with and without the new flags absent); with --plinth round the PNG differs and has opaque pixels in the bottom band; --aspect 16:9 gives width:height 16:9.
acceptanceCriteria: Default output unchanged (asserted)
Plinth and aspect options produce the asserted image properties
The CLI usage line documents the new flags

userStories.title: Scene composer for dioramas (showcase_scene.mjs)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want many generated GLBs placed together on one plinth and rendered as one scene, so the material shows assets working together the way ccore's game GIF does.
steps: Create scripts/showcase_scene.mjs `--layout FILE --out DIR [--width 1920 --height 1080] [--frames N] [--name NAME]`. Layout JSON: {plinth: {shape: 'round'|'square', size_m, top, side}, camera: {yaw, pitch, fov, zoom}, items: [{glb, x, z, rot_y_deg, height_m?, scale?}]}. Each item is loaded, its lowest point set to y = 0 (plinth top) and its centre (x/z) moved to (x, z); `height_m` scales it uniformly to that height, otherwise `scale` (default 1, the asset's own metres). Never edit geometry or materials.

Before rendering, check overlaps: compute each placed item's x/z footprint box and print a warning line per overlapping pair (ids and overlap area); `--strict` makes overlaps an error. Print one JSON summary line {items, overlaps, missing}. A missing GLB is an error naming the path.

Lighting, shadows and tone mapping as in showcase_render.mjs (reuse by importing shared code into a small module, scripts/showcase_common.mjs, rather than copying). Still: DIR/NAME.png at width x height on a transparent background. With --frames N: DIR/NAME_orbit/0000.png... a full 360-degree camera orbit around the plinth centre; animated items play their first clip over the orbit.

Tests (Chromium): a layout of three makeGlb assets renders, the summary reports 3 items and 0 overlaps; two items at the same x/z report 1 overlap and fail with --strict; a missing GLB fails with its path; --frames 4 writes 4 frames.
acceptanceCriteria: Overlap, missing-file and strict cases are asserted
Shared lighting code lives in scripts/showcase_common.mjs and showcase_render.mjs output stays unchanged
No GLB geometry or material is modified (asserted by re-parsing a placed GLB's mesh count and material count)

userStories.title: Launch film (promo_film.sh)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want a 25-30 s 1920x1080 MP4 that strings the slides, the diorama orbits and the turntable together, for X, LinkedIn and YouTube.
steps: Create scripts/promo_film.sh using ffmpeg only: sequence = title card (release/v1/promo/out/cover_1280x640.png scaled and padded to 1920x1080, 2.5 s) -> village orbit (frames from scenes_out/village_orbit, 20 fps, composited over the dark studio gradient image release/v1/promo/bg_1920x1080.png which the script renders once via make.mjs or an ffmpeg gradient) -> slides 2-5 (2.5 s each, slow 4% zoom-in) -> harbour orbit -> turntable_1200.mp4 centred on the gradient (3 s) -> end card (slide 1 text replaced by the Ollama command and 'Apache 2.0 · Built on Muse Glimmer 30B', 3 s). 0.4 s crossfades between parts. H.264, yuv420p, CRF 18, faststart, no audio track.

`--dry-run` prints the ffmpeg command lines without running them. Test (tests/py/test_promo_film.py) runs --dry-run against a temp dir of dummy PNGs and asserts the part order, the crossfade count and that no network URL appears.

userStories.title: GLB name sanitizer (Blender 5.2 crash on float-suffixed names)
userStories.description: As a user importing a Meshwright GLB into Blender, I want it not to crash Blender. Root cause found 22 Nov 2026 (14 crash reports, ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Blender-*.ips): the model sometimes names parts with raw float coordinates, e.g. 'sack_0.5_1.0499999999999998' or 'bed_plank_0.09999999999999998'. Blender 5.2.0 treats '.<digits>' at the end of a name as a duplicate-number suffix, std::stoi overflows (out_of_range) in BLI_string_split_name_number and Blender aborts (SIGABRT). 15 of 540 distill GLBs are affected (for example x0025, x0131, x0148, x0149, x0158, x0198); x0149 and x0158 are in the village diorama.
steps: Create scripts/glb_names.mjs exporting `sanitizeNames(buf) -> {buf, renamed: [{kind, index, from, to}]}`. It rewrites only the `name` strings of nodes, meshes, materials, animations and scenes in the JSON chunk (pad with spaces to 4 bytes, BIN chunk untouched, total length updated, like scripts/glb_ground.mjs). Rule: every decimal number in a name with more than 3 fractional digits is rounded to at most 3 (trailing zeros dropped, -0 becomes 0): 'sack_0.5_1.0499999999999998' -> 'sack_0.5_1.05'; then, if the name still ends in '.' followed by digits whose value exceeds 999999, replace that last '.' with '_'. If a rewrite makes two names of the same kind equal, append '_2', '_3'... Names that need no change stay byte-identical; a GLB with no changes is returned unchanged (same buffer).

Never touch indices, accessors, buffers, materials' values or animation channels (channels target node indices, so renaming nodes is safe). CLI: `node scripts/glb_names.mjs --in FILE --out FILE` prints one JSON line {renamed: N}; `--check FILE[,FILE...]` only reports files that would change, exit 0.

Apply it in the delivery path: scripts/glb_ground.mjs (or the step in scripts/glb_generate.py that writes the picked GLB) runs sanitizeNames after grounding, and the generator records `renamed_names: N` per attempt in result.json. Do not re-run or rewrite any existing runs/ output.

Tests (tests/js/glb_names.test.mjs, registered in tests/js/index.js) with makeGlb: the two example names above are rewritten as stated; 'dormer_-3.5' and 'window_frame_2.2_2.8' are unchanged; a name ending '.12345678901' gets '_' instead of '.'; a collision gets '_2'; an untouched GLB is the same buffer; parseGlb ok and the same triangle count after sanitizing; an animated fixture keeps its channel target indices.

docs/15-release.md: a short 'Known issue: Blender 5.2 crash on float-suffixed names' note (cause, 15/540, fixed in the generator output; GLBs exported by hand from the v1 page can still carry such names, so a v2 prompt should say 'never put decimal numbers in names'). Do not edit prompts/.
acceptanceCriteria: All listed rewrite, no-change, collision and animation cases are asserted
`node scripts/glb_names.mjs --check` over runs/imp/distill/*/asset.glb (read only) reports 15 files, recorded in notes

userStories.title: Blender import proof (blender_import_check.py)
userStories.description: As the owner, I want proof that the GLBs import into a real 3D tool, like ccore's Godot screenshots, made headless so it is repeatable.
steps: Create scripts/blender_import_check.py, run as `blender -b --factory-startup --python scripts/blender_import_check.py -- --glbs FILE[,FILE...] --report FILE [--render FILE --layout release/v1/promo/scenes/village.json]`. For each GLB: reset to an empty scene, `bpy.ops.import_scene.gltf`, record ok/error, object count, mesh count, total triangles (evaluated), material count and action (animation) count. Write a JSON report with one row per GLB and totals.

With --render: import every item of the layout, place it as the layout says (same placement rules as showcase_scene.mjs), add a sun light and a camera matching the layout camera, and render one EEVEE (or Workbench if EEVEE is unavailable headless) 1920x1080 image. Also write a second image that looks like Blender: Workbench render with the default grey studio look and the outliner-style list of imported object names drawn as a text overlay is NOT needed; instead render Workbench with 'random' object colours so separate parts are visible.

Run it on all GLBs used by the two layouts and the six slides; write release/v1/promo/out/blender/report.json, blender_village_eevee.png and blender_village_parts.png. If blender is not on PATH, the script's wrapper test is skipped with a clear message (do not fail the gate).
Test (tests/py/test_blender_import_check.py): when blender exists, import one makeGlb-equivalent tiny GLB written by the test (two boxes, one animation) and assert ok, mesh count 2, action count 1.
acceptanceCriteria: report.json lists every GLB with ok true or a specific error (any failure is reported, not hidden)
Both Blender renders exist at 1920x1080
The test passes or is skipped only because blender is missing
`bash scripts/check.sh` passes (syntax checks, pytest, node tests; offline)
Any script flag or behaviour you changed or added is described in README.md or the doc the story names
userStories.notes: Blender crashed repeatedly in the first attempt (12:17-12:20): root cause is float-suffixed part names, see US-008. Now: run each GLB import in its own `blender -b` subprocess (one crash must not stop the others), import a temp copy sanitized with scripts/glb_names.mjs (names only, geometry untouched), and in report.json record per GLB `raw_names_crash_risk` (true when sanitizeNames would rename anything) plus the import result of the sanitized copy. Any remaining crash is reported as ok=false with the signal, never hidden. Kill any leftover Blender process at the end.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. No network, no hf upload, no ollama, no git push, never commit. READ ONLY: runs/imp/distill/*/asset.glb, runs/imp/distill/*/result.json, runs/imp/adaptive/best/glimmer-v3-adaptive/glb/*.glb, bench/glb/briefs.jsonl, bench/distill/briefs.jsonl. WRITE ONLY: scripts/showcase_*.mjs, scripts/promo_film.sh, scripts/blender_import_check.py, release/v1/promo/ (except out/cover_1280x640.png, out/social_1080.png, out/showcase_grid.png, out/how_it_works_1600x640.png, out/turntable_*, out/unfiltered_eval_48.png, which are published and must not change), tests/, docs/15-release.md. Never touch data/, out/ (repo root), eval/, .env, .venv, prompts/. Never modify a GLB's geometry, materials or animation: only position, rotate and uniformly scale whole assets in a scene. Tests use GLBs built in the test (tests/js/glb_util.mjs makeGlb) and temp dirs.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use fixtures under tests/fixtures and mocked HTTP. Never call Baseten, Meta, Hugging Face or any remote service from a story, a test or a script you run. The only network use allowed is `npm install` and `.venv/bin/pip install` of packages the story names.
Never commit, push, tag or publish. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.

Never delete, overwrite or reformat anything under data/, out/, eval/, .env or .venv. They are the owner's data (a long Glimmer generation run may be writing data/raw right now). Tests write only to temporary directories.

Do not start long jobs. Any command that would run more than about 5 minutes (corpus generation, training, GGUF conversion, evals) is written as a script plus docs and left for the owner. A live smoke call to the local Ollama is allowed only if the story says so, with at most 2 briefs, and must skip cleanly when Ollama is down. Never rent GPUs or run `runpodctl` with anything that creates a pod.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests and the doc the story names. Do not change prompts/system.txt: every existing raw answer was generated against it.

Match the surrounding code: short comments that explain why, argparse CLIs, resumable file-per-item outputs, no new dependency the story does not name. Python runs with `.venv/bin/python`; Node scripts are ESM `.mjs` (Node 22).
Three.js stays pinned at 0.160.0 and the validator keeps serving the local copy in place of the CDN URL.
Python scripts must stay importable without heavy deps: import torch, transformers, trl or peft only inside functions or under `if __name__ == '__main__'` so pytest can import them.
Record only real results. Never invent pass rates, token counts, timings or costs; where a number is unknown write 'not measured'.
Debug output goes to data/ or a temp dir, never into scripts/ or docs/.
If the spec is wrong or impossible, do the closest thing that works and explain the difference in `notes`. If you cannot finish a story, set `notes` to why and stop; do not mark it passing.

The completion tag is matched literally by the harness. Write it only when every acceptance criterion holds. When a criterion cannot hold yet, never type the tag, not even inside a sentence saying you are not using it; write 'no completion signal this iteration' instead.
